chapter_theme: Not killing is the first of all goods, ranked explicitly above truthfulness and above all renunciation. It is absolute, holding even at the cost of one's own life and regardless of any gain, and the chapter ends with the fate of those who kill.
structure_note: Parimelazhagar divides the chapter: its excellence (321-323), that only the path containing it is good (324), the height of the one who keeps it (325), its benefit (326), the fault of killing (327-328), and the harm to killers (329-330).

321.reading: If you ask what virtuous action is, it is not killing; killing brings all the other kind of deed.
321.nuance: பிறவினை, 'other deeds', leaves the wrongness to be inferred. Parimelazhagar takes it as a claim about results: the suffering killing yields exceeds that of all other sins combined.

322.reading: Sharing one's food and sustaining many lives is the chief of all that the authors have gathered.
322.nuance: Inside a chapter on not killing, the crown goes to a positive act of feeding, so non-harm here isn't only refraining. Parimelazhagar assigns the summary to renunciants, Manakkudavar says it is good for all faiths, and Kalaignar reads an egalitarian creed into it.

323.reading: Good beyond compare is not killing; following behind it, not lying is good.
323.nuance: A rare moment of the Kural ranking two of its own highest claims. Parimelazhagar recognizes this: since 297 and 300 raised doubt about which is greater, this verse settles it, and it can do so because truth depends on results and therefore shifts.

positions.position: The verse exists to settle a doubt that the chapter on truth raised.
positions.quote: இரண்டு அறந்துள்ளும் யாது சிறந்தது என்று ஐயம் நிகழுமன்றே!

324.reading: If you ask what is called the good path, it is the way that keeps in view not killing anything at all.
324.nuance: The question form follows 291 and 321, as if the Kural is defining terms. யாதொன்றும் is wide, and Parimelazhagar says it takes in even one-sensed life. சூழும் makes it a matter of constant attention rather than a single vow.

325.reading: Among all who renounced out of fear of their condition, the one who fears killing and keeps not killing in view is chief.
325.nuance: Two fears are set side by side with the repeated அஞ்சி, one about one's own state and the other about another's life. The second outranks the first.

positions.position: He is the highest within the class of renunciants, who differ by sect.
positions.quote: கொலைப் பாவத்தை அஞ்சிக் கொல்லாமை ஆகிய அறத்தை மறவாதவன் உயர்ந்தவன்.

positions.position: He may stay a householder and still be above all who renounce.
positions.quote: கொல்லாமையைச் சிந்திப்பான் தலைமை யுடையவன்; இல் வாழ்க்கையில் நிற்பினும்,

326.reading: Death, the devourer of life, does not advance on the days of one who lives by not killing.
326.nuance: The symmetry is exact: the one who won't kill is not killed, and the killer of all refrains here.

positions.position: It promises a full allotted span without interruption, which gives time for knowledge and release.
positions.quote: இப் பேரறம்செய்தான் தானும் கொல்லப்படான்; படானாகவே, அடியிற்கட்டிய வாழ்நாள் இடையூறின்றி எய்தும்

positions.position: Death doesn't come because there will be no further birth.
It is a tribute: death itself hesitates, in awe.

327.reading: Even if your own life should go, do not do the deed that takes away another's sweet life.
327.nuance: இன்னுயிர் gives the other's life the word for sweetness, while one's own is just உயிர். This is the Kural's hardest statement of the rule, and it allows no exception of necessity.

positions.position: The case is a creature that would kill you: even then, because killing increases sin. He rejects a reading about ritual expiation.
The case is killing for medicine in mortal illness, which some people hold is no fault.
positions.quote: உயிர்க்குக் கேடுவருங் காலத்து நோய்க்கு மருந்தாகக் கொல்லுதல் குற்ற மன்று என் பார்க்கு, இது கூறப்பட்டது.

328.reading: However great the gain that would bring good, gain that comes by killing is the lowest for the worthy.
328.nuance: The verse mentions no sacrifice. That whole issue comes from the older commentators and through them Pope's gloss.

positions.position: The issue is Vedic sacrifice, valid for householders seeking heaven and base only for those seeking release, so injunction and prohibition don't clash.
positions.quote: துறக்கம் எய்துவார்க்கு ஆம் ஆயினும், வீடு எய்துவார்க்கு ஆகாது

positions.position: Killing in sacrifice is also not acceptable, as the great seek release and let ritual go.
It is any killing that would produce great benefit, and sacrifice isn't mentioned.

329.reading: People whose work is killing are of base occupation in the eyes of those who discern what baseness is.
329.nuance: Baseness is assigned by work, not birth, as both Parimelazhagar and Manakkudavar stress, though the word புலை itself carries caste weight. Parimelazhagar's claim here that sacrifice isn't killing at all fits awkwardly with his note on 328.

positions.position: The phrase 'whose work is killing' shows that killing in sacrifice isn't killing.
positions.quote: 'கொலை வினையர்' என்றதனான், வேள்விக் கண் கொலையன்மை அறிக.

330.reading: Those in wretched bodies, leading an evil and failing life, they say, are people who separated life from body.
330.nuance: என்ப, 'they say', is the verse's own hedge. It doesn't mention a former birth, which Parimelazhagar and Manakkudavar supply. Its logic runs backward from a sufferer to his guilt, and that makes it one of the more troubling claims in this section.

links.note: 330 reports that the diseased and destitute are paying for their killings. 1062 rages that if people must beg to live, the world's maker should perish. One explains misery as deserved, and the other refuses to accept it at all.
320 says that all pain rests on those who caused pain, looking forward. 330 turns this around and reads a past killing from present suffering.

327 forbids taking life even to save one's own. 550 likens the king's execution of murderers to weeding a crop. Here the Kural's most absolute rule meets its statecraft, and it does not reconcile them.

259 explicitly mentions sacrifice but only of oblations, and sets not killing above it. 328 doesn't mention sacrifice, but the commentators find animal sacrifice there. That shows how a commentary tradition can place a controversy in the text.
972 says that birth is alike for all and distinction comes from the work done. 329 applies this to killing: base by occupation. The commentators' emphasis on 'by work' follows the same principle.

source_issues: 330: Manakkudavar's text has தீய பனை வாழ்க்கை, likely a misprint for தீய வாழ்க்கை or similar.
